title: Female borrowers who mention reducing health and hazard risks to the family may fund faster.
Female borrowers using the specific phrase 'hardworking entrepreneur' may fund faster.
Providing precise ages for children in the pitch text is associated with increased funding speed for women.
The inclusion of gratitude markers or expressions of thanks to the lenders in the pitch text is associated with slower funding speeds for women.
Female borrowers who list specific technical skills or training programs may fund more slowly.
Mentioning specific loan amounts in local currency (PHP) may accelerate funding for women.
Female borrowers who include their own age in the pitch may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who specify the goal of sending children to college may fund faster.
Technical business specificity may accelerate funding for women but decelerate it for men.
Female borrowers who provide specific logistical or technical details, such as land size or transport, may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that provide concrete financial figures or specific inventory lists fund faster regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who use generic template language fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention a specific town or city in their pitch fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention the goal of building savings fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention a history of successful loans from NWTF fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
